chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily Ali (peace be upon him) emancipated a Christian slave of his, and he embraced Islam when he emancipated him.

key_terms.أَسْلَمَ: Embraced Islam, became a Muslim — the spiritual consequence described here follows the act of emancipation
key_terms.أَعْتَقَ: Emancipated/freed from slavery — a legally significant act in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيّاً: A Christian (Nasrani) — indicating the slave was a dhimmi or non-Muslim at the time of emancipation

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim emancipate a non-Muslim slave according to Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) freed a Christian slave, who then immediately accepted Islam upon his emancipation. This narration establishes a legal precedent regarding the emancipation of non-Muslim slaves by Muslims, demonstrating that such emancipation is valid even if the slave is not a Muslim at the time, and that the spiritual transformation of the freed person may follow from the act of liberation itself.
word_analysis: so he became a Muslim/embraced Islam
